title: Compact-support Frobenius transport commutes with coefficient extension
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and let $X_0$ be separated of finite type over $k_0$. Put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, let $a_X:X\to s$ be the projection, $\gamma=(z\mapsto z^q)^{-1}$, $g=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$, and $h=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. Let $u:A\to B$ be any unital map of finite commutative rings annihilated by integers prime to $p$. Work in the ordinary uncompleted constant-coefficient derived categories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], and put $T_Z=(-)\otimes_A^LB$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Let $D^b_{ctf}$ have the bounded constructible, finite-Tor-amplitude meaning of [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude].

Fix a compactification $c_0=(X_0\xrightarrow{j_0}\overline X_0\xrightarrow{r_0}\operatorname{Spec}k_0)$, meaning $j_0$ is an open immersion, $r_0$ is proper, and their composite is the structure map [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Write $c=(j,r)$ for its base change to $k$, and use $Ra^c_{X!}=Rr_*j_!$. For $R=A,B$ and $N\in D^b_{ctf}(X,R)$ put $H_R(N)=\Gamma(s,Ra^c_{X!}N)$, where point sections are applied termwise [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. Write $P_R=Lg_R^*$ and use the canonical pullback-composition identification $d_{m,R}:L(g^m)_R^*\xrightarrow{\sim}P_R^m$ [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition].

For these arbitrary finite rings define $e_R: Lh_R^*Ra^c_{X!}\to Ra^c_{X!}P_R$ as the ambient proper exchange mate of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange] for $r$, followed by the canonical open-square comparison [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change]. Define $\iota_{R,M}:\Gamma(s,M)\to\Gamma(s,Lh_R^*M)$ by restriction of sections along $h$, insertion into the inverse-image colimit, and the map to derived pullback. This is the finite-ring formula of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport], used here for every $R$. Put
$$\tau_{R,N}=\Gamma(s,e_R(N))\circ\iota_{R,Ra^c_{X!}N},\qquad
\tau^m_{R,N}=H_R(d_{m,R}^{-1})\circ\tau_{R,P_R^{m-1}N}\circ\cdots\circ\tau_{R,N}\quad(m\geq1).$$
The latter has exactly $m$ single-transport factors and has target $H_R(L(g^m)_R^*N)$.

For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ let $C_c(K):H_A(K)\otimes_A^LB\xrightarrow{\sim}H_B(T_XK)$ be the canonical compact-support coefficient comparison of [det-prop-scalar-six-compact-support], followed by point sections and their canonical scalar-extension comparison [lem-trf-point-complex-scalar-extension]. Use the ordinary finite-ring incarnations, obtained by primary decomposition and the finite-discrete coefficient identifications [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-condensed-ring-constant, lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-scheme-ring-constant]. Let $c_{v,K}:Lv_B^*T_XK\xrightarrow{\sim}T_X(Lv_A^*K)$ be the inverse pullback coefficient comparison [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback]. Since $g^m$ is an automorphism of the scheme $X$, $L(g^m)_A^*K$ again lies in $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, so $C_c(L(g^m)_A^*K)$ is defined. Then for every $m\geq1$,
$$
H_B(c_{g^m,K}^{-1})\circ C_c(L(g^m)_A^*K)\circ(\tau^m_{A,K}\otimes1)
=\tau^m_{B,T_XK}\circ C_c(K)
$$
as morphisms $H_A(K)\otimes_A^LB\to H_B(L(g^m)_B^*T_XK)$. This equality is natural in $K$. It holds for the semilinear $g,h$ specified above. If another representative of $Ra_{X!}$ is used, transport the displayed maps through its canonical compactification comparison with $c$; the equality still holds. No Weil structure on $K$, coefficient flatness of $B$ over $A$, or trace-formula equality is assumed.

proof.text:
Put $F_R=Rr_{*,R}j_{!,R}$, $Q_R=Lh_R^*$, and $G_R=L\bar g_R^*$, where $\bar g=\operatorname{id}_{\overline X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$. The two squares $r\bar g=hr$ and $\bar g j=jg$ are Cartesian: base-changing an isomorphism gives its inverse-image square. In particular all three horizontal arrows are isomorphisms of schemes, irrespective of $k$-linearity. Use $\mu_v=c_v^{-1}:T Lv_A^*\to Lv_B^*T$ and $t:T_{\overline X}j_{!,A}\to j_{!,B}T_X$. By [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] these are the canonical tensor comparisons, and the $\mu$'s respect composition. All coefficient encodings here are identified using [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-condensed-ring-constant, lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-scheme-ring-constant].
For use of the finite $\ell$-primary coefficient results, choose an integer $n$ prime to $p$ annihilating both rings. The Chinese-remainder integers $e_\ell$ modulo $n=\prod_\ell\ell^{a_\ell}$ satisfy $\sum e_\ell=1$, $e_\ell e_{\ell'}=0$ for $\ell\ne\ell'$, and are preserved by the unital map. Thus every module sheaf or complex is the finite direct sum of its $e_\ell$ parts; all the displayed maps preserve these parts. Tensor, pullback and adjunction units/counits are computed componentwise (apply each $e_\ell$ to their defining equations). An equality on every primary component is therefore an equality before decomposition; a zero component contributes only zero maps. We henceforth perform the argument on one nonzero primary component.

proof.text:
Write $q:T_sRr_{*,A}\to Rr_{*,B}T_{\overline X}$ for the coefficient map of [det-prop-scalar-six-direct-image]. Its counit equation is
$$\varepsilon^B_{T N}\circ Lr_B^*(q_N)=T(\varepsilon^A_N)\circ c_{r,Rr_{*,A}N}.$$
The same node supplies naturality and the normalization on the ambient derived categories. Here $r$ is a proper $k$-morphism between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, so its hypotheses hold. No application of its $k$-morphism assertion to $h,g,\bar g$ is being made. Put
$$b_K=Rr_{*,B}(t_K)\circ q_{j_{!,A}K}:T_sF_AK\longrightarrow F_BT_XK.$$
By [det-prop-scalar-six-compact-support], this is precisely the specified compact-support coefficient isomorphism on $D^b_{ctf}$, and $F_R$ takes this domain to $D^b_{ctf}(s,R)$. The scalar-extended input is in the same domain by [det-prop-scalar-six-ctf]. Under point sections the comparison in the item is consequently $C_c(K)=\Gamma(b_K)\circ S_{F_AK}$, where $S$ is [lem-trf-point-complex-scalar-extension].

proof.text:
Let $E_R:Q_RRr_{*,R}\to Rr_{*,R}G_R$ be the ambient exchange of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-coefficient-exchange-mates] to the two adjunctions $Lr_R^*\dashv Rr_{*,R}$ for each $R=A,B$, the horizontal pullbacks $Q_R,G_R$, and the four scalar-extension functors. Its push comparisons are $q$, whose counit equations were specified in Step 2; its pull comparisons are $c_r$, and its horizontal comparisons are $\mu_h,\mu_{\bar g}$. Its pull cube commutes by [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback](1): the two paths compare coefficient extension with pullback along the equal composites $r\bar g=hr$, using their canonical composition comparisons. Its exchange counit equations are exactly the defining transpose in [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange]. The resulting square is
$$Rr_{*,B}(\mu_{\bar g,N})\circ q_{G_AN}\circ T_s(E_A(N))\circ c_{h,Rr_{*,A}N}
=E_B(T_{\overline X}N)\circ Q_B(q_N).\tag{P}$$
Both sides go from $Q_BT_sRr_{*,A}N$ to $Rr_{*,B}G_BT_{\overline X}N$. The abstract mate theorem has no geometric linearity or invertibility hypothesis on exchange. Thus (P) applies to the semilinear horizontal maps, and to non-flat $B/A$.

proof.text:
Let $o_R:G_Rj_{!,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{!,R}P_R$ be [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change]. In this square $G_R,P_R$ are reindexing along scheme isomorphisms, by [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image]. On the extension presheaf of [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf], reindexing relabels a summand, and the tensor comparison sends a summand element $x\otimes b$ to that same element in the relabelled summand. Tensor then relabel and relabel then tensor give identical maps, including zero summands. After sheafification this proves
$$o_B(T_XK)\circ G_B(t_K)\circ\mu_{\bar g,j_{!,A}K}
=j_{!,B}(\mu_{g,K})\circ t_{P_AK}\circ T_{\overline X}(o_A(K)).\tag{O}$$
The tensor maps here are exactly those of [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback](1),(2); extension by zero is degreewise and exact by [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. To compute their derived versions take a flat-term K-flat representative, using [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]; the pullback/tensor computation of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and the termwise open scalar comparison identify the two sides with the sheafified maps just computed. Thus (O) is an equality of the specified derived maps, without treating tensor by $B$ as exact.

proof.text:
By definition $e_R=Rr_{*,R}(o_R)\circ E_R$. Apply (P) to $N=j_{!,A}K$, postcompose by $Rr_{*,B}(o_B(T_XK)\circ G_B(t_K))$, and use naturality of $E_B$ for $t_K$. In the other path use (O), followed by naturality of $q$ for $o_A(K)$. Substituting $b=Rr_{*,B}(t)q$ gives
$$F_B(\mu_{g,K})\circ b_{P_AK}\circ T_s(e_A(K))\circ c_{h,F_AK}
=e_B(T_XK)\circ Q_B(b_K).\tag{E}$$
Its source is $Q_BT_sF_AK$ and its target is $F_BP_BT_XK$. This pasting uses the two computed squares and naturality only; in particular it identifies the actual proper/open exchange rather than an arbitrary base-change isomorphism.

proof.text: We may check the point square on bounded constant finite-projective models. Here is why these models cover its domain, using statements rather than the proof of the point-comparison node. For $M\in D^b_{ctf}(s,A)$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin] gives a bounded etale origin. By [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk](1), with inverse given by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-algebraically-closed-etale-sheaf-constant], that etale complex is a termwise constant realization of an ordinary complex $V$. By [lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module], $M\simeq c_AV$ on the pro-etale site. Constant sections give $\Gamma_s c_AV=V$: for a constant module its sheaf is locally constant functions, and evaluating at the one-point final object recovers exactly its value. This description is supplied by [lem-cbc-continuous-functions-fpqc-sheaf]; the constant-presheaf map is a local bijection (restrict to the open fibres), so [lem-cbc-set-presheaf-sheafification-local-bijection] identifies its sheafification. The argument applies in each degree. Thus $V\simeq\Gamma_sM$, which is perfect by [lem-trf-point-complex-scalar-extension]; choose a bounded finite-projective model $V'\simeq V$. We have $c_AV'\simeq M$. By [lem-sfb-constant-realization-derived-scalar-extension](1), scalar change on this model is the termwise tensor, with all comparison maps canonically normalized on constant sections.

source.place: Final sentence, coefficient naturality; explicit agent expansion

proof.text:
For $M=c_AV'$ in Step 6, the finite-ring recipe of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] takes a constant section $x$ to its restriction along $h$, then to its inverse-image class $[x]$, and then to $[x]\otimes1$. The pullback structure map fixes constant ring sections and commutes with $A\to B$ by [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image](3). Both paths of the coefficient square therefore send $x\otimes b$ to $[x]\otimes b$. By the normalization of $S$ in [lem-trf-point-complex-scalar-extension] and of the pullback comparison in [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback], this is
$$S_{Q_AM}\circ(\iota_{A,M}\otimes1)=\Gamma(c_{h,M})\circ\iota_{B,T_sM}\circ S_M.\tag{I}$$
The calculation is degreewise, with the same differential. It holds on every $M$ via Step 6: restriction and colimit insertion commute with sheaf maps, and $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ is natural, so the point transport is natural on complexes. The exactness of sections [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact] and of reindexing makes it natural after quasi-isomorphisms are inverted as well. Naturality of $S$ and $c_h$ then carries the equation through $c_AV'\simeq M$. This proves (I) for every finite-ring component, not only the coefficient rings listed in the original point-transport definition.

proof.text:
Use (I) at $M=F_AK$, then (E). Naturality of $S$ for $e_A(K)$ first gives
$$\begin{aligned}
&H_B(\mu_{g,K})C_c(P_AK)(\tau_{A,K}\otimes1)\\
&=\Gamma\bigl(F_B(\mu_{g,K})b_{P_AK}T_s(e_A(K))\bigr)S_{Q_AF_AK}(\iota_{A,F_AK}\otimes1)\\
&=\Gamma(e_B(T_XK))\Gamma(Q_B(b_K))\iota_{B,T_sF_AK}S_{F_AK}\\
&=\Gamma(e_B(T_XK))\iota_{B,F_BT_XK}\Gamma(b_K)S_{F_AK}\\
&=\tau_{B,T_XK}C_c(K).
\end{aligned}\tag{1}$$
The penultimate line is the naturality of point transport established in Step 7, applied to $b_K$. Naturality of $S$ is [lem-trf-point-complex-scalar-extension]. Every point comparison is defined because $F_AK$ and its isomorphism pullbacks are in the stated finite-Tor constructible domain. Equation (1) is natural in $K$, since each of its constituent maps is natural.

proof.text:
Write $\Theta_{R,r,K}=\tau_{R,P_R^{r-1}K}\cdots\tau_{R,K}:H_RK\to H_RP_R^rK$, with $\Theta_{R,0}=1$. Define $u_0=1$ and
$$u_{r+1}=P_B(u_r)\circ\mu_{g,P_A^rK}:T_XP_A^{r+1}K\longrightarrow P_B^{r+1}T_XK.$$
Set $B_r=H_B(u_r)C_c(P_A^rK)$. We prove
$$B_r(\Theta_{A,r,K}\otimes1)=\Theta_{B,r,T_XK}C_c(K)\tag{2}$$
by induction. At $r=0$ this is the identity. For the induction step apply (1) to $P_A^rK$ and postcompose with $H_B(P_Bu_r)$. Naturality of $\tau_B$ for $u_r$ changes the resulting right side to $\tau_{B,P_B^rT_XK}B_r$. Precompose with $\Theta_{A,r,K}\otimes1$ and substitute the induction hypothesis. The recursion for $u_{r+1}$ gives the left side of (2) at $r+1$, and the definition of $\Theta$ gives its right side. All $P_A^rK$ remain bounded constructible of the same Tor amplitude: isomorphism reindexing preserves the defining finite local data and exact tensor tests by [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image]. Naturality of $\tau_B$ follows by composing the natural point transport with the natural exchange.

proof.text:
Let $V_R=L(g^m)_R^*$ and $d_{m,R}:V_R\to P_R^m$ be the specified comparison. Coefficient/pullback composition compatibility in [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback](1), iterated $m$ times, gives
$$u_m\circ T_X(d_{m,A})=d_{m,B}\circ\mu_{g^m,K}.\tag{D}$$
Here the canonical parenthesizations are those of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]; [lem-trf-derived-pullback-coherence] identifies successive reassociations, so these are precisely the $d_m$ in the statement. Postcompose (2) at $r=m$ with $H_B(d_{m,B}^{-1})$. By (D) and naturality of $C_c$ for $d_{m,A}^{-1}$ its left side becomes
$$H_B(\mu_{g^m,K})C_c(V_AK)\bigl(H_A(d_{m,A}^{-1})\Theta_{A,m,K}\otimes1\bigr).$$
The right side becomes $H_B(d_{m,B}^{-1})\Theta_{B,m,T_XK}C_c(K)$. Substitute the definitions of $\tau_R^m$ and $\mu=c^{-1}$; this is exactly the displayed equality of the item, with exactly $m$ single-transport factors. All identities are natural. Reassemble the primary components of Step 1. Finally, replacing $F_R$ by another representative and transporting all displayed maps through its canonical comparison with $c$ conjugates both sides by the same endpoint isomorphisms; cancellation preserves the equality. This last clause uses precisely the transport convention in the item and makes no assertion about an independently chosen exchange.
